liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Comes A Time** (5 reviews): Reviewer found Comes A Time a nice highlight of an otherwise good-not-great show; Reviewer calls Comes A Time terrific and says it alone makes the download worthwhile [11][13][17][18][20]
- **Broken Arrow** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Broken Arrow among the good moments; Phil's voice sounded great on Broken Arrow [11][16]
- **So Many Roads** (1 review): Reviewer says Jerry almost always nailed So Many Roads in the 90s, without the meltdowns seen elsewhere [16]
- **Here Comes Sunshine** (1 review): Second set has some vocal miscues in Here Comes Sunshine [20]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): Samson & Delilah, along with Way to Go Home and Saint of Circumstance, is rated very good [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Drums with Jerry**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **The Rain Song**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1994-10-09.111984.akg.datbrad.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 167 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd94-10-09.sbd.braverman.17357.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 164 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound quality is described as solid [13]
- **gd1994-10-09.sbd.miller.34562.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 164 min; rated 3.12/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: Transition between discs 2 and 3 is seamless [4]
- **gd1994-10-09.nak300.bleich.GEMS.93876.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [6]. Said about its sound: Tape flips were crossfaded, with plugins and EQ applied to the transfer [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer had poor seats at the arena, still called the Cap Centre; a friend spotted something on Bobby's head [11]
- Reviewer recalls the Cap Centre's great atmosphere and laments it was demolished and replaced by a strip mall [12]
- Reviewer drove from Philly on a Sunday night, heading back to Toronto afterward; the Cap Centre crowd was edgy [17]
- Reviewer ranks this among the better shows of the fall tour, though some performances fall short [13]
- Apart from a few first-set tunes and Comes A Time, reviewer finds the performance pretty average [15]
- Reviewer sees it as a decent show from the last fall tour, a solid year, and attended every stop [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1994-10-09.111984.akg.datbrad.flac16**: taped by datbrad; transferred by datbrad; source: (OTS) AKG460s/CK8s(PAS)>B-18s>FP-11s>DAP20(16/48) Digital [1]
- **gd94-10-09.sbd.braverman.17357.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD ?> C4> CD> SHN via Billy Schools encoded by Peter Braverman [3]
- **gd1994-10-09.sbd.miller.34562.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) -> ? -> 3rd Gen Cassette D [4]. Also: Recorded with AKG 460/CK61 microphones to DAT, then transferred to CD; Cassettes were supplied by Gary Field and played on a Nak cassette deck lent by macdaddy [4]
- **gd1994-10-09.nak300.bleich.GEMS.93876.flac16**: taped by John Bleich; transferred by Brian Green; Evan K.; source: Nak 300's > D6 [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 10/9/1994 Washington DC Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_941009_ex.html) [24]
